message.content: {"mechanism_id":"delta-f-floor-memory-decay","target_component":"M_F/M_CR success-memory update (Lehmer/weighted-mean aggregation)","observed_evidence":{"task_id":"TASK-01","trace_path":"none","function":"F21","seed":0,"metric":"success_rate","observed_value":1.0},"causal_hypothesis":"Zero-improvement successes (delta_f=0) enter the memory with weight 0 in the weighted mean but still shift Lehmer mean of F because Lehmer uses raw F values regardless of weight, so equal-fitness trials inflate M_F and bias future sampling without contributing fitness signal.","algorithmic_change":"Replace the single memory update with a two-tier scheme: samples with delta_f>0 update M_F/M_CR normally; samples with delta_f=0 update a separate shadow memory M_F0/M_CR0 that is blended into the active memory with a decay factor rho<1, so zero-improvement samples only weakly influence sampling.","mathematical_rule":"if delta_f > 0: M_F = Lehmer(S_F); M_CR = weighted_mean(S_CR, w=|delta_f|); else: M_F0 = (1-rho)*M_F0 + rho*F_trial; M_CR0 = (1-rho)*M_CR0 + rho*CR_trial; M_F = (1-alpha)*M_F + alpha*M_F0; M_CR = (1-alpha)*M_CR + alpha*M_CR0 with alpha=0.1, rho=0.2","expected_effect":"Reduces M_F inflation on F21 and F7 late runs, lowering stall_gen and preventing memory drift toward high F/CR from neutral trials.","failure_prediction":"On unimodal or easy functions where delta_f=0 is rare, alpha blending adds noise and may slightly slow convergence; if rho too high, shadow memory dominates and reintroduces the original bias.","ablation_plan":"Compare (a) baseline L-SHADE, (b) delta_f>0 gate only, (c) proposed shadow-memory blend, (d) proposed with alpha=0 (shadow ignored). Measure stall_gen, success_rate, and M_F trajectory on F7/F21 seeds 22/33.","nearest_known_methods":"Weighted Lehmer memory in L-SHADE; success-history adaptation in SHADE; elite memory in jSO; exponential smoothing of control parameters.","implementation_requirements":"Add M_F0, M_CR0 arrays and alpha, rho constants; branch memory update on delta_f sign; log both memories per generation; no change to selection or mutation."}
